# Music Library Manager — Requirements Document (Reverse-Engineered)

*Compiled from the implementation as of 2026-08-27 — not from the original README brief, which describes an earlier, partially-superseded design. Present tense = "the system currently does this." Generated by the Architect stage of this repo's dev-loop; update it as the system evolves rather than letting it drift.*

---

## 1. Data Model

1.1. A **Project** represents a scanned folder — either a recognized DAW project or a plain container folder — and has: id (relative path from music root), name, absolute path, optional marker path (the file/package that identified it as a DAW project), optional DAW type, optional human-readable detection method, `hasVideo`/`hasImage` flags, a status, a list of tags, a score, first-seen/last-seen timestamps, a removed flag, and a `contentModifiedAt` timestamp.

1.2. An **AudioFile** represents one scanned audio file and has: id (relative path from music root), absolute path, relative path, filename, extension, size, optional created-at, modified-at, containing folder, optional owning project id, status, tags, score, first-seen/last-seen timestamps, and a removed flag.

1.3. **Status** is one of five values: `unknown`, `draft`, `needs_mixing`, `done`, `released` — for both Projects and Audio Files independently.

1.4. **Score** is either `null` (unset) or an integer from 1 (worst) to 5 (best), for both Projects and Audio Files.

1.5. **Tags** are free-text, user-defined strings, case-insensitively deduplicated, shared across a single global tag vocabulary and attached independently to Projects and Audio Files (many-to-many).

1.6. `contentModifiedAt` on a Project is the later of the project folder's own filesystem mtime and its DAW marker file's mtime (e.g. the `.als` file, which updates on every save) — distinct from `lastSeenAt`, which only reflects scan bookkeeping.

1.7. Every scanned row (Project or AudioFile) tracks `firstSeenAt`, `lastSeenAt`, and `isRemoved`, so a file/folder that disappears from disk is soft-deleted (marked removed) rather than hard-deleted, preserving its user-entered status/tags/score in case it reappears.

## 2. Scanning & Indexing

2.1. The scanner recursively walks a configured root folder using async filesystem APIs, tolerating one bad file/folder (permission error, broken symlink, race condition) without aborting the whole scan — each failure is recorded as an error in the scan result.

2.2. The scanner recognizes audio files by extension: `.wav`, `.aiff`, `.aif`, `.mp3`, `.m4a`, `.flac`, `.ogg` (configurable list).

2.3. The scanner ignores, everywhere: dot-directories, `node_modules`, `.git`, `.Trash`, `.Spotlight-V100`, `.fseventsd`, `.TemporaryItems`, `$RECYCLE.BIN`, `.DS_Store` files, and AppleDouble (`._*`) files.

2.4. The scanner classifies a directory as a **DAW project** using, in priority order: (a) a child directory whose name ends in a package-style extension (currently only `.logicx` → Logic Pro) — the package itself is the project; (b) a directly-contained file with a known DAW project extension (`.als`→Ableton, `.cpr`→Cubase, `.ptx`/`.ptf`/`.pts`→Pro Tools, `.flp`→FL Studio, `.reason`/`.rns`→Reason, `.song`→Studio One, `.rpp`→Reaper, `.bwproject`→Bitwig); (c) fallback: an exact-name marker subfolder ("Ableton Project Info") when no project file is present.

2.5. Every visited folder (except the scan root) gets its own Project row — whether or not it's a recognized DAW project — except a plain folder nested *inside* a recognized project, which is omitted from the folder list (a project nested inside another project still gets its own row).

2.6. An audio file is associated with the nearest ancestor directory recognized as a DAW project; files outside any recognized project remain unassociated (`projectId` undefined).

2.7. A folder's `hasVideo`/`hasImage` flags are set if a video/image file exists anywhere in its subtree, including nested folders that aren't listed as rows of their own (e.g. inside a Samples folder) — detected via ancestor-propagation from every found video/image file up to the scan root.

2.8. On each scan, a file is treated as: new (not previously seen — inherits its project's current score/tags immediately), modified (size or modified-at changed — filesystem fields are refreshed but user-set status/tags/score are preserved), unchanged (only `lastSeenAt` is touched), or removed (previously active, not seen this scan — marked removed).

2.9. Comparable removal/change detection applies to Projects: any previously-active project not observed in the current scan is marked removed.

2.10. A scan records aggregate statistics: root path, start/finish time, duration, folders scanned, audio files found, DAW projects found, new/modified/removed file counts, and a list of per-path errors. The most recent scan run is retrievable.

2.11. Scanning is strictly read-only: it never renames, moves, deletes, or modifies any file on disk.

## 3. Scan Settings (Toggleable Ignore Rules)

3.1. "Exclude Samples folders" (default: on) skips any folder literally named "Samples" (case-insensitive) everywhere in the tree, since such folders are typically imported/library material rather than the user's own production audio.

3.2. "Exclude Backup folders" (default: on) skips any folder literally named "Backup" (case-insensitive) everywhere in the tree, since Ableton auto-generates these to hold autosaved project versions.

3.3. Both toggles are persisted (survive app restart) and only take effect on the next scan.

3.4. Regardless of the Samples-folder exclusion setting, a project's own Contents/Duplicate-detection views still read the Samples folder live from disk — the exclusion only controls what gets indexed into the Audio Files list, so the Files tab isn't polluted with imported samples.

## 4. Scan Exclusions (Per-Folder Opt-Out)

4.1. The user can pick specific subfolders (by browsing a folder tree) to exclude from scanning entirely; the scanner does not descend into an excluded folder or anything beneath it.

4.2. Selecting a folder to exclude automatically un-excludes (and visually disables/greys) any of its already-excluded descendants, since excluding the parent already covers them.

4.3. Exclusions are relative paths from the configured music root, persisted across restarts, and applied on the next scan.

4.4. Changing the configured music root clears all saved scan exclusions, since they were only meaningful relative to the previous root.

## 5. Project Folders View

5.1. Displays every active (non-removed) Project as a paginated, filterable, sortable table with columns: selection checkbox, name/id, Type (DAW label or "Folder"), Status, Tags, Score, Audio Files (count), Media (video/image icons), and a "Reveal in Finder" action.

5.2. The Type column shows the detected DAW's display name (e.g. "Ableton", "Logic Pro") or "Folder" for a plain container; hovering shows the detection method (e.g. "Ableton — detected via .als file").

5.3. Clicking a row opens a detail panel (see §8) showing the project's contents, duplicates, DAW marker files, and editable status/tags/score; clicking outside the panel, or its close button, closes it.

5.4. "Reveal in Finder" opens the project's folder in macOS Finder without navigating away from the table (its click is isolated from row-selection).

## 6. Audio Files View

6.1. Displays every active audio file as a paginated, filterable, sortable table with columns: selection checkbox, play button + filename/extension, Status, Tags, Project (id), Score, Location (containing folder path, truncated with full-path tooltip), and Modified date.

6.2. Clicking a row (outside the play button/checkbox) opens a detail panel (see §8) with the file's size, full path, project association, and editable status/tags/score.

6.3. A library-wide stats summary ("Metrics") shows total file count, files with status Draft, and files with no score set, refreshed after any scan or edit; it also shows the change count (new+modified+removed) from the most recent scan.

## 7. Filtering & Sorting

7.1. Both Projects and Files views support: a debounced (250ms) text search (matches name/id for projects; filename or relative path for files), multi-select Status filter (OR'd), multi-select Score filter (OR'd, including an explicit "Unscored" option matching `score IS NULL`), and multi-select Tags filter (OR'd — matches any of the selected tags).

7.2. Both Files and Projects tables support sorting by Name, Score, and Modified date via clickable column headers (Files additionally sorts by Location/Folder); clicking a header sorts by that column ascending, clicking the same header again toggles to descending, and clicking a different header switches the sort to that column. Each sort header is a button with `aria-label="Sort by <Column>"` and the header cell carries `aria-sort` ("ascending"/"descending"/"none"). There is no separate toolbar sort control — column headers are the only sort mechanism for either table.

7.3. "Modified" sort for Projects orders by `contentModifiedAt` (the later of folder mtime / DAW marker mtime) — not raw folder mtime and not `lastSeenAt`.

7.3a. Sorting by Score treats an unset (`null`) score as the lowest possible value: unscored rows sort first in ascending order and last in descending order (SQLite's default `NULL`-ordering behavior, relied on as-is rather than special-cased).

7.4. Changing any filter or the search text resets pagination back to page 1.

7.5. A "Clear" control (always visible, disabled when no filter/sort is active) resets search, status, score, tag, and sort state in one action.

7.6. The result count for each view ("N of Total") is shown next to the filter bar.

7.7. If an edit or rescan shrinks the result set below the current page, the view automatically clamps back to the last page that still has data. (A filter change cannot trigger this: per §7.4, any filter change resets the page to 1 first, which structurally preempts the clamp — confirmed via `useAudioFiles`/`useProjects` test coverage, see `docs/COVERAGE.md` §7.7.)

## 8. Detail Panels

8.1. A slide-in side panel (files and projects each have their own) shows full detail for the selected item, is dismissible via close button, Escape key, or clicking the backdrop, and auto-focuses its close button when opened.

8.2. Both panels let the user change Status (single-select pill group), Score (five-dot click-to-set / click-again-to-clear editor), and Tags (add via Enter or blur, remove via a per-tag "×") — each field saves immediately (optimistic UI update with rollback on failure) and shows a "Saving…" indicator while in flight.

8.3. The Project detail panel additionally shows: DAW type badge, "Detected via …" note (when applicable), a duplicate-detection warning block (see §10) when matches exist, a list of nested DAW project files when the folder contains more than one, and a read-only, expandable tree of the folder's actual on-disk contents (files and subfolders), always reflecting the live filesystem rather than the database.

8.4. The File detail panel additionally shows: formatted file size, full relative and absolute path, and "Reveal file in Finder" / "Reveal project in Finder" actions (the latter only shown when the file belongs to a project).

## 9. Batch Operations

9.1. Both views support multi-row selection via per-row checkboxes and a "select all visible" checkbox in the header; selection is cleared whenever filters, page, or the active tab change.

9.2. A "Batch Edit" button (enabled only once 2+ rows are selected) opens a batch panel offering: set-score (applies immediately to every selected item, **overwriting** each item's existing score) and add-tag (applies immediately, **adding** to each item's existing tags — union, not replace).

9.3. Batch score edits on Projects cascade the same score onto every audio file belonging to each selected project. Batch tag edits on Projects cascade the added tags onto every file belonging to each selected project.

9.4. Batch edits on Files re-sync each affected file's project's score (recomputed max) and tags (recomputed union) afterward.

## 10. Duplicate Detection

10.1. For a selected DAW project, the system searches for other active projects made with the *same* DAW type whose Samples-folder contents substantially overlap with this project's Samples-folder contents — a signal that one project's sample folder was copied from/into the other.

10.2. Sample files are matched by (filename, size) pair, case-insensitive on filename; a folder is only searched for "Samples" content by name match (any depth) or, at the project's top level only, a folder named "Imported" (deep "Imported" folders are excluded, since Ableton's own Max-for-Live device cache uses that name and would produce false positives).

10.3. A candidate is flagged as a possible duplicate if it shares at least 3 matching sample files **and either**: (a) the match ratio (matches ÷ the smaller of the two projects' sample counts) is at least 0.6 unconditionally, **or** (b) the two projects' names are equal after trimming whitespace and lowercasing, and the match ratio is at least 0.5 (a relaxed bar that only applies when the name itself is already strong independent evidence — the absolute 3-sample floor is never relaxed, and differently-named pairs are never affected by the 0.5 bar). Each match reports which of these signals contributed via a `matchReasons` list (`"sameName"`, `"sampleOverlap"`, or both).

10.4. A plain container folder (no DAW type) is never treated as a duplicate candidate or target, and two projects are never compared if one's folder is an ancestor of the other's (that's containment, not duplication).

10.5. Matches are excluded if the candidate project is currently scan-excluded (via §4) or belongs to a different DAW.

10.6. Results are sorted by descending match ratio and displayed with project name, path, matching-sample count, overlap percentage, and a "Same name" badge when `matchReasons` includes `"sameName"`.

## 11. Playback

11.1. Clicking a file's play button in the Audio Files table starts (or pauses, if already playing that file) in-app playback via a fixed player bar docked to the bottom of the viewport; clicking a different file's play button switches playback to it.

11.2. The player bar shows filename, relative path, play/pause, stop (resets to 0:00), a seekable progress slider, elapsed/total time, and a close button that stops and dismisses the bar.

11.3. Audio is streamed from the server with HTTP Range support, enabling seeking without downloading the whole file first; a playback or unsupported-format error is shown inline in the player bar.

11.4. Table/list content adds bottom padding while the player bar is visible so the last rows aren't hidden behind it.

11.5. The audio-streaming endpoint only ever serves the path stored in the database for that file id (populated exclusively by the scanner) — it cannot be used to read arbitrary paths from the request. As defense-in-depth against a bad `path` value entering the DB by some other means, the endpoint additionally refuses (server-side) to stream any resolved path outside the currently configured music root, even if the DB row itself points outside it, mirroring §13.4's guard.

## 12. Score & Tag Linking (Project ↔ Audio File)

12.1. Editing a single file's score or tags recomputes its parent project's score and tags from scratch, based on **all** of the project's current active files: score becomes the **maximum** score among them (or `null` if none are scored), tags become the **union** of all their tags. This means a value no longer held by any file naturally drops off the project.

12.2. Editing a project's score or tags **cascades** onto every active file it contains: the project's score **overwrites** each file's score; the project's tags are **added** to each file's tags (union, not replace).

12.3. These two directions are independent, one-way operations (file→project recompute, project→file cascade) that never call each other, so no infinite ping-pong is possible.

12.4. When a new audio file is discovered inside a project during a scan, and that project already has a score and/or tags, the new file immediately inherits them rather than starting blank.

## 13. Settings & Configuration

13.1. The music root ("Prod Folder") defaults to `~/Music` (or the `MUSIC_ROOT` env var) but can be overridden at runtime via a text field or a native macOS folder picker; the override is validated (must exist and be a directory) and persisted across restarts.

13.2. A dedicated panel lets the user choose which top-level (and nested) subfolders to include/exclude from scanning (§4), and trigger a scan directly from that panel.

13.3. A separate Settings panel exposes the two scan-time ignore toggles (§3) with save-state feedback ("Saving…"/"Saved"/"Failed").

13.4. "Reveal in Finder" is refused (server-side) for any path outside the currently configured music root, even if requested directly.

13.5. The Settings panel's Confirmation Settings section exposes 6 independent, persisted toggles gating a typed-text confirmation step before a destructive/bulk action runs: "Confirm tab deletion" (type the tab's exact name), "Confirm copy"/"Confirm move"/"Confirm delete" (type the literal word COPY/MOVE/DELETE, for the Copy/Move/Delete operations described in §16), and "Confirm status deletion"/"Confirm tag deletion" (type the status's/tag's exact name before it can be removed from the global Statuses & Tags catalog, a separate editable-catalog panel not otherwise covered in this document). Each toggle is off by default; when on, the relevant action's confirm dialog requires the exact text to be typed (case-sensitive) before the confirm button enables. Removing a tag from a single file's or project's own tag list (§8.2) is a separate, lighter-weight action and is never gated by any of these toggles.

## 14. Theming

14.1. The UI supports three themes — ProFolder (default, the app's own brand palette/typography), Light, and Dark — selected via a header dropdown (`ProFolder`/`Light`/`Dark`, in that order), persisted in `localStorage`, and applied without a flash by being set (via a `data-theme` attribute on the document root) before first paint. A one-time migration reads any pre-existing legacy dark/light preference on first load under the new mechanism.

14.2. All interactive components (badges, panels, tables, inputs) have distinct dark/light color treatments rather than relying on a single palette. Theming is expressed entirely via CSS custom-property tokens (defined per `[data-theme]` in `frontend/src/index.css`) and consumed through plain Tailwind utility classes — no component holds theme-conditional JS logic (`isDark`/`isProFolder`-style props or branching), enforced by a permanent regression test (`frontend/src/test/isDarkIsProFolderSweep.test.ts`). `ThemeSelector.tsx` is the sole, deliberate exception, taking a single `theme` string prop where a color/font-weight distinction genuinely can't be expressed through CSS alone. A number of ProFolder-specific color roles (danger/notice/success/info/warning surfaces, status badge/pill colors, chrome text/border tiers, the modal scrim, tag-chip background, and a secondary ink tier) are still interim placeholders reusing the Light theme's resolved values, each flagged in-code, pending a future visual-design pass to pick final ProFolder-branded values — this is a deliberate, user-approved intermediate state, not a missing feature.

14.3. The app displays a splash screen for 1 second on every app load/refresh (a UI placeholder for a future scan-on-startup feature, not yet wired to a real scan) — a full-viewport overlay in the current theme's background color, with the ProFolder logo centered and "Syncing…" text beneath it.

14.4. The app's logo mark (three sheared color slabs on a dark tile) appears in the header and as the browser favicon; the header and browser tab title read "ProFolder."

## 15. Custom Tabs

15.1. In addition to the default "Project Folders" and "Audio Files" tabs, the user can create any number of **custom tabs**, each a named, saved view over either Projects or Audio Files (never both) filtered to a fixed Status/Score/Tags subset. A leftmost "+" button in the tab bar opens a creation modal offering: a name, a type choice (Project Folders or Audio Files), and optional Status/Score/Tags filter pickers (the same multi-select controls as the default tabs' filter bars, including the "Unscored" score option).

15.2. A custom tab's Status/Score/Tags membership is **locked at creation time** — it is the tab's permanent filter criteria and cannot be edited afterward; there is no edit UI, only create and delete.

15.3. Within a custom tab, free-text search and sort order remain live and interactive on top of the tab's locked subset, exactly as in the default tabs — but neither is part of the tab's saved definition: the Status/Score/Tags pickers themselves are hidden while a custom tab is active, since that criteria is fixed.

15.4. A custom tab's search text and sort order reset to their defaults every time the user navigates away from that tab and back — not only on app cold start. Each custom tab's table/panel is only rendered while it is the active tab, so switching away unmounts it and switching back remounts a fresh instance with no memory of the prior search or sort state.

15.5. Custom tabs support the same row interactions as their underlying type's default tab: opening the detail panel, editing Status/Score/Tags from it (with the same project↔file linking behavior as §12), batch edit, pagination, and "Reveal in Finder".

15.6. Playback is global, not per-tab: there is a single audio player bar shared across the whole app, so starting playback from within a custom Audio Files tab, then switching to another tab (default or custom), leaves the same file playing uninterrupted.

15.7. Each custom tab is shown in the tab bar with its name and its own "×" delete button; clicking "×" opens a confirmation dialog, and deleting is permanent (no undo, no soft-delete). Deleting the tab that is currently active falls back to the default "Project Folders" tab. The confirmation dialog can optionally require typing the tab's exact name before it confirms — see §13.5 for the Settings toggle that gates this; off by default.

## 16. Copy, Move & Delete

16.1. Copy, Move, and Delete are available for a single audio file (from the File detail panel), a single project folder (from the Project detail panel), and for a multi-row batch selection (from the Batch Edit panel) on either view — in both the default "Project Folders"/"Audio Files" tabs and any custom tab of either type. Each operation can optionally require a typed-text confirmation (typing the literal word COPY/MOVE/DELETE) before running — see §13.5 for the Settings toggles that gate this per operation; off by default.

16.2. Delete moves the item to the macOS Trash via Finder (`MacTrashService`, AppleScript `tell application "Finder" to delete`) — it is reversible, not a permanent filesystem deletion. This is an explicit product decision, not an oversight.

16.3. Copy and Move destinations are restricted to folders inside the currently configured music root — an explicit product decision. The destination folder picker (`DestinationFolderPicker`) is populated from `GET /api/folders/tree` and only ever shows folders inside the root; the backend independently re-validates containment (`isWithinRoot`, symlink-safe) on every copy/move route regardless of what the picker sent, and rejects (400) a request whose resolved destination falls outside it.

16.4. Moving or copying a project folder relocates/duplicates its whole subtree — the project itself, every nested sub-project inside it, and every audio file contained anywhere in that subtree — as a single atomic database transaction (`moveProjectSubtree`/`cloneProjectSubtree` in `src/database/repositories/subtreeRekey.ts`), performed by rekeying/cloning the existing rows' id/path fields in place rather than removing and re-discovering them via a rescan. Status, tags, and score are preserved unchanged on every affected row at the new location.

16.5. Moving or copying a single audio file similarly preserves its status, tags, and score (`moveFile`/`cloneFile` in `src/database/repositories/audioFileRepository.ts`), and its project association is recomputed from its new location (nearest DAW-classified ancestor project, or none) rather than carried over from the old location.

16.6. Name-collision behavior differs by operation: Move rejects (409, no partial write) if an item with the same name already exists at the destination, for both files and project folders. Copy never rejects on a name collision — it auto-renames Finder-style instead (`kick.wav` → `kick copy.wav` → `kick copy 2.wav`; `My Project` → `My Project copy` → `My Project copy 2`), for both files and project folders.

16.7. Batch Copy/Move/Delete report success and failure per item, not all-or-nothing: each selected id is processed independently server-side, and a failure on one item (not found, name collision, path outside root, filesystem error) does not roll back or block items that already succeeded. The batch panel surfaces a summary banner reflecting the actual succeeded/failed counts.

16.8. Known, deliberately deferred limitations (not yet fixed):
- A destination directory that does not yet exist on disk produces a misleading error message ("Refusing to operate on a destination directory outside the configured music root") from the copy/move routes — the response is safe (400, no partial writes), but the wording is inaccurate, since a nonexistent path and a genuinely outside-root path both fail closed the same way through `isWithinRoot`'s `realpath`-based check with nothing distinguishing the two causes.
- `POST /api/files/batch/copy` does not deduplicate a repeated id within a single request — it produces two independent auto-renamed clones instead of collapsing them. `batch/move` and `DELETE /batch` don't have this problem (the second occurrence of the same id naturally fails, since the row no longer exists there after the first occurrence is processed).
- `POST /api/projects/batch/move` (and `batch/copy`) process a batch's ids sequentially, re-reading each project's current path from the database on every iteration; if a batch selection contains both a project and one of its own nested sub-projects, moving the ancestor first rekeys the descendant's row as a side effect, then the loop moves the already-relocated descendant again — silently flattening it out of its parent, with the outcome depending on id order rather than erroring. The UI's own batch-selection flow defends against this (`BatchEditPanel.tsx`'s `excludeNestedProjectIds` drops any selected project that is a descendant of another selected project before sending the request), but the raw API itself has no such guard for a non-UI caller.

- Data model: `src/models/{Project,AudioFile,Tag,Score,ProjectDuplicate,CustomTab}.ts`, `src/database/migrations/001–010_*.sql`
- Scanning: `src/scanner/{walk,ignoreRules,dawDetector,dawTypes,mediaDetector,duplicateDetector,projectDetector,audioDetector,folderTree,scanner}.ts`
- API: `src/api/routes/{files,projects,config,scan,folders,reveal,stats,tags,customTabs}.ts`, `src/api/server.ts`
- Custom tabs: `src/database/repositories/customTabRepository.ts`, `frontend/src/components/{CreateCustomTabModal,DeleteTabConfirmDialog,CustomFilesTabPanel,CustomProjectsTabPanel}.tsx`
- Copy/Move/Delete: `src/services/{FileOpsService,TrashService}.ts`, `src/database/repositories/subtreeRekey.ts` (plus `moveFile`/`cloneFile` in `audioFileRepository.ts`), `frontend/src/components/{CopyMoveDeleteDialog,DestinationFolderPicker}.tsx`

- Config: `src/config/{musicRoot,scanSettings,config}.ts`

## Appendix B — Flags: Unfinished, Inconsistent, or Dead Code

1. **Stale `dist/` build output referencing removed "export confidence" concept.** The compiled `dist/` tree (gitignored, not tracked) still contains `dist/src/scanner/exportClassifier.js`, `dist/tests/exportClassifier.test.js`, and references inside `dist/src/database/repositories/audioFileRepository.js`, `dist/src/scanner/scanner.js`, and even the built frontend JS bundle — all from before the migration to the score system. **Source (`src/`, `tests/`) is fully clean** — the only remaining references are in migration files `001_init.sql` and `008_scoring.sql`, which is correct (they're the historical record of the schema change, and `008` explicitly documents dropping `is_export_candidate`/`export_confidence`/`likely_exports`/`likely_samples`/`unknown_confidence`). Recommend simply rebuilding (`npm run build`) before relying on `dist/`, or deleting it — no source cleanup is needed.
2. **`FileTagService` (`src/services/FileTagService.ts`) is entirely unused/unwired.** It defines an interface and a `NoopFileTagService` placeholder for a future macOS Finder-tag sync (explicitly deferred per its own comment, matching README §8/Phase 4), but nothing in `src/api/server.ts` or elsewhere imports or instantiates it. It is inert scaffolding, not a bug, but it's dead code as far as the running app is concerned.
3. **`MusicLibraryService` (README §9/Phase 5, Music.app integration) was never implemented** — no such file exists anywhere in `src/`. This matches the README's explicit "later phase" framing, so it's a planned-but-not-built feature rather than a regression, but worth confirming it's not silently expected by any other code (it isn't).
4. **`ProjectWithFiles` type (`src/models/Project.ts`) is defined but never used** anywhere else in the codebase — the actual project-detail API response shape is defined ad hoc in `frontend/src/api/client.ts` (`ProjectDetail`) instead. Minor unused-type cleanup candidate.
5. **An entire unrelated project is committed inside this repo:** `Real-Time Claims Review UI/` (39 tracked files — a Figma-Make-generated "claims review" React app, `.figma/`, its own `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, etc.) has nothing to do with Music Library Manager and is checked into git at the repo root (present since the first commit). This looks like an accidental commit from an unrelated project/tool run and should probably be removed from this repository.

Likely an intentional simplification, but worth confirming with the product owner since Files view *does* expose name-sort via a clickable column header.~~ **RESOLVED** (Sorting improvements feature, `docs/TODO.md` item 4): the old toolbar "Sort: Modified" button has been removed entirely and `ProjectsTable` now exposes clickable, ascending/descending-toggling column headers for Name ("Project Folder"), Score, and Modified — the same column-header sort mechanism Files already had, closing the UI asymmetry this item flagged. See §7.2 above.
7. ~~**`getLibraryStats` "Draft" metric only counts files with status exactly `draft`**, not, e.g., `needs_mixing` — this matches the current 5-value status enum but the metric tile is easy to misread as "not yet done"; worth confirming this is the intended definition now that status has more granularity than the original two-state (`draft`/`finished`) model.~~ **RESOLVED** (Metrics per-status breakdown feature): `getLibraryStats` was renamed to `getFileStats` and no longer collapses statuses into a single "Draft" tile — it (and the new sibling `getProjectStats`) return a full per-status breakdown (`EntityStats.byStatus`, one count per currently-known status catalog key) for both Audio Files and Projects, closing the single-tile ambiguity this item raised.

## Appendix C — Test Coverage Status

*Superseded by a full clause-by-clause audit (Task 9 of `docs/TODO.md` item 1) — see
`docs/COVERAGE.md` for the complete §1–§14 verdict table (85 rows, ~113 individual clauses,
with citations). §15 Custom Tabs was added in a later cycle and is covered separately by its own
§15 verdict table in that same file — it is not included in the §1–§14 figures above. This
section is now just a short pointer plus the genuinely-still-open items; do not treat the bullets
previously here as current, several were stale by the time Task 9 ran.*

**Previously listed here as open, now confirmed closed:**
- §2.4's DAW-classification priority-collision case (package ext > project-file ext > marker
  subfolder, when both a project-file and a marker-subfolder would otherwise apply to the same
  directory) — closed in Task 3, `tests/dawDetector.test.ts:95`.
- §5.4/§8.4's "Reveal in Finder" path-containment guard — closed in Task 3,
  `tests/finderService.test.ts:22-40` + `tests/revealRoute.test.ts:50-69`.
- "API route/HTTP-level behavior is entirely untested" — no longer accurate as a blanket claim;
  `tests/revealRoute.test.ts`, `tests/batchRoutes.test.ts`, and `tests/audioStreamRoute.test.ts`
  all spin up the real Express app via `supertest`/`createServer` and hit routes over HTTP. (Not
  every route has HTTP-level coverage — see `docs/COVERAGE.md` §10.1/§2.10c for two that don't —
  but the categorical claim was wrong.)
- §11.5's audio-streaming path safety had **zero** coverage (not just "same pattern as §13.4,
  untested" — it turned out to have no containment guard implemented at all, a real gap, not
  just an undertested one). Found via mutation-testing during Task 9's audit, then fixed and
  hardened in **Task 9.4**: `GET /:id/audio` now shares the same `fs.realpathSync`-based
  root-containment guard as §13.4's reveal endpoint (`isWithinRoot`, exported from
  `src/config/musicRoot.ts` — relocated there from `src/services/FinderService.ts` by Task 9
  follow-up item 13's cohesion cleanup), fails closed, and is symlink-safe (an initial prefix-only
  fix was found bypassable via a symlink inside the root pointing outside it; the escalated fix
  closes that too). See `tests/audioStreamRoute.test.ts` (7 tests) and the reworded §11.5 above.

**Still genuinely open** (full detail and citations in `docs/COVERAGE.md`; grouped here, see
`docs/TODO.md` item 1's Task 9 follow-up list for the actionable next-loop breakdown):
- Projects-view default sort order (name, ascending) is exercised implicitly but never
  explicitly asserted as "the default when no `sortBy` is given" (`docs/COVERAGE.md` doesn't
  carry this as its own row — it's a `projectRepository.test.ts` general-query side effect, not
  a named requirement clause — but it's worth folding into any future §7 test pass).
  Cross-referenced: no §7.2/§7.3 row explicitly claims this either; treat as a minor documentation
  gap rather than a numbered clause.
- §10.1/§10.6b — the duplicate-detection HTTP route and its UI rendering (project-detail-panel
  duplicate-warning block, §8.3) have zero coverage at their actual layer; only the underlying
  pure functions are unit-tested.
- §2.10c — `GET /api/scan/last` (most-recent-scan-run retrieval) has zero coverage at any layer.
- §12.3 — the "two link-sync directions never call each other, no ping-pong" claim is verified
  only by reading `linkSync.ts`'s two exports, no regression test guards against a future
  regression re-introducing a cycle.
- §7.5 is flagged **REQUIREMENT-SUSPECT**, not just undertested: `FilterToolbar.tsx:200-211`
  always renders a "Clear" control (merely `disabled` when no filter is active), not
  conditionally shown as the requirement's wording implies — this may be a requirements-doc
  inaccuracy rather than a code gap; worth confirming with the product owner before writing a
  test against either interpretation.

See `docs/COVERAGE.md` for the full row-by-row breakdown, including every `PARTIAL`/`NONE` clause
